basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 41:1; Genesis 24:13 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 264. Quid est quod Pharao dixit: Putabam me stare super flumen (Gen. XLI, 1)?--'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 264. Quid est quod Pharao dixit: Putabam me stare super flumen (Gen. XLI, 1)?-- Resp. Id [ Ms., Idem] est quod in alio loco legitur: Ecce ego super fontem aquae sto (Gen. XXIV, 13). Hoc genere locutionis et in psalmo dicitur: Qui fundavit terram super aquam [Ms., aquas ]. [Non coguntur homines putare sicut navem natare terram super aquas]. Secundum hanc [enim] locutionem [recte] intelligitur, quod altior sit terra quam aqua. Altius quippe ab aquis sustollitur, ubi habitant terrena animalia.
